From: Samir Patel <samir@tidehealth.ai>

Subject: Redwood demo — SLO targets & pilot handoff

Marcus — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions before we lock the pilot MAP: 

High-level goals (what we need validated in pilot):
- 95th p99 latency for single-turn prompts <= 320ms for 512-token responses.
- Sustained throughput target: 120 qps for our baseline model family (2.7B distill).
- Burst concurrency: up to 550 concurrent sessions for 30s bursts during traffic spikes.
- Streaming: must support chunked streaming with backpressure so our web client can partially render tokens; we need connection-level flow control and a mechanism to drop long-running requests gracefully.

Attached is a spreadsheet with our nominal and worst-case SLO rows (tide-requested-slos.xlsx). Two specific questions:
1) Which Redwood model/quant profile would you recommend to meet the latency/throughput targets at our budget? We prefer a quantized 4-bit option if that preserves accuracy.
2) For streaming backpressure, how does Redwood surface partial tokens + error fallback in the SDK? We need a clear client-side pattern for resuming vs aborting.

Next steps we want in the MAP: proposed pilot scope, measurement harness, acceptance gates, and a rough runbook for failover to a lower-cost variant if latency breaches. Can you send a short MAP and owners by end of day Monday?

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, Tide Health

Thanks Samir — great list and very clear. High-level response + proposed MAP attached (redwood-slo-map-v1.xlsx). Summary below so everyone can triage quickly: 

Short answers to your two questions:
- Model/quant: for 2.7B use-case we recommend rwd-2.7b-q4f16 (dynamic 4-bit, per-channel) as the first pass. It preserves generation quality for your test prompts in our evals and reduces memory enough to hit your latency target on T4-like nodes. If you need lower unit-cost we can run a q3a profile but we should validate quality on the prompt set.
- Streaming/backpressure: Redwood streams tokens over the standard chunked HTTP SSE path in the SDK. We expose a per-request state enum (STREAMING, ABORTED, FALLBACK) and a streaming checkpoint ID you can persist; the client can request a resume for a partial generation using the checkpoint ID, or we can return a short fallback that uses cached completions. The attached MAP includes the client pattern and example pseudo-code.

Proposed pilot MAP (high level):
1) Kickoff & scope alignment (week 0) — confirm 20 canonical prompts, acceptance thresholds, and success metrics. Owner: Marcus Lin (Sales SE).
2) Run synthetic load runs to calibrate qps & concurrency on a dedicated pool (week 1) — Owner: Redwood Ops (Ben Carter) + Tide infra.
3) Short end-to-end pilot with streaming integration (week 2) — validate p95/p99 and streaming semantics against the client harness. Acceptance gate: p99 <= 320ms and <1% failure/retry ratio.
4) Fallback & failure runbook test (week 3) — simulate node loss and validate graceful fallback to q3 variant or cached responses.

Action items for Monday (EOD):
- I attached a draft MAP (redwood-slo-map-v1.xlsx). Please review and highlight any changes.
- Can you confirm the 20 canonical prompts and indicate which of the 3 candidate models you prefer for the first run?

Attaching: redwood-slo-map-v1.xlsx (MAP + measurement plan)

—

Key items we need to confirm internally (please reply inline):
- Hardware profile: target instance family? Samir listed T4-like in the notes; confirm whether we gate on a2-highmem / g5 / T4 equivalents for the pilot.
- Batching policy: we should test both continuous batching (prefetch window 20ms) and strict low-latency path (no batching). Which will we surface in the pilot config?
- KV cache sizing: for the checkpoint resume behavior, estimate RAM + GPU memory overhead for rwd-2.7b-q4f16 at their concurrency burst (550).
- Test harness: Ben, can your team spin up the synthetic driver that simulates streaming with per-connection backpressure? We'll need a 1M-event stress run and 10k sustained qps smoke.

I attached a short pilot-runbook.md draft with the test commands and measurement endpoints. If we can validate the qps/latency envelope in a 2-hour synthetic run we can commit to the MAP. If not, we'll propose a constrained pilot with reduced concurrency and explicit fallback.

Please treat this as high priority — I want to turn this around to Samir by Monday EOD.

Samir — looping back with confirmation and concrete next steps. Thanks for the patience while we validated internal capacity. Quick notes and what we want to run in week 1: 

Hardware & profiles:
- Pilot hardware: 4 x A10G-equivalent nodes (dedicated pool) to start. We'll run a calibration sweep and may scale to 6 nodes if needed.
- Model profile: rwd-2.7b-q4f16 as Marcus suggested. We'll bring up q3a as a lower-cost fallback if quality drift appears.

Planned validation runs (week 1):
1) 2-hour synthetic burst run: drive 120 qps sustained with 30s 550-concurrency bursts to validate concurrency plumbing and cache behavior. Measurement points: p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, GPU utilization, retry ratio.
2) Streaming integration: run the streaming harness against the SDK pattern Marcus provided; validate resume semantics and checkpoint IDs. We'll exercise client aborts, resumes, and fallback to cached completions.
3) Failure injection test: simulate one node drop and validate automatic fallback to lower-cost variant + routing policy.

Owners & schedule:
- Redwood Ops (Ben Carter) — provision pool, run synthetic stress, collect metrics, share results.
- SE integration (Grace Oconnor) — help Tide infra implement streaming client pattern and validate checkpoint resume path.
- Tide (Samir) — provide 20 canonical prompts and an initial acceptance set by EOD Mon (21 Jun).

Deliverables by end of week 1:
- Calibration report (CSV + Grafana dashboards link)
- Updated MAP with the run outputs and pass/fail flags
- Runbook entry for fallback behavior and expected timelines for scale-up

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync Thursday to walk through the calibration results. Marcus — please share the MAP link and your prompt list when you get them.
